selected.lesson_subject: Central SNAT map selection with dynamic external IP-feed source objects
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: external-resource address feed -> central-snat-map orig-addr/orig-addr6 reference -> ordered SNAT rule selection after firewall-policy match -> IP-pool translation
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: refresh external IP feed; match source against feed in central SNAT table; choose first matching map by source/destination/interface/protocol/port; translate source after security policy
selected.failure_class: feed unavailable or stale; wrong address-family object; map shadowing/order; central NAT disabled or per-policy NAT assumed
selected.evidence_pattern: external-resource refresh/status; diagnose firewall iprope list 10000d; matching central-snat-map entry; session/NAT table showing translated source
selected.remediation_path: validate feed type and address family; verify feed fetch and parsed addresses; enable central NAT; check top-down map ordering and interfaces; confirm policy admits flow; inspect session translation
selected.question_fingerprint: distinguish policy acceptance from central-SNAT map selection and diagnose a stale or shadowed dynamic feed
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: external IP feed -> address external-resource -> ordered central SNAT map -> firewall session translation -> WAN

selected.lesson_subject: FortiManager script object types and execution-target boundaries: CLI, Tcl and Jinja
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: ADOM-scoped script object -> type selector CLI/Tcl/Jinja -> Run Script on target constraint -> platform/build validation -> target-specific execution context
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: create script in Device Manager or Global Database ADOM; choose type and execution target; validate syntax/platform; select device/database/policy package; run and inspect execution history
selected.failure_class: script type incompatible with target; Global Database restriction; platform/build syntax mismatch; script runs against device database rather than live device
selected.evidence_pattern: script type and Run Script on fields; validation result; script execution history; device task status; resulting device/database diff
selected.remediation_path: select type/target pair deliberately; validate on actual platform/build; scope script to intended ADOM and device group; compare device database and live running config before/after
selected.question_fingerprint: identify which execution target is valid for CLI versus Tcl versus Jinja and what a successful validation does not prove
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: ADOM script definition -> type/target gate -> validator -> device database/ADOM database/direct FortiGate target -> execution history

selected.lesson_subject: FortiAnalyzer forwarding-mode log export: reliable TCP buffering, filters, exclusions and masking
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: client-side forwarding profile -> destination type FAZ/syslog/CEF/output plugin -> device/log filters and field exclusions/masking -> TCP reliable buffer or UDP -> remote receiver
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: create forwarding entry on source FortiAnalyzer; select server type and destination; optionally filter devices/logs and mask fields; enable reliable TCP; forward real-time or near-real-time; remote FAZ authorizes forwarded devices
selected.failure_class: transport UDP loss; TCP buffer saturation; unsupported server type/port; filters suppress needed events; remote device remains unauthorized
selected.evidence_pattern: get system log-forward; forwarding status; remote connection; sender buffer/backlog; receiver device authorization and incoming log timestamps
selected.remediation_path: separate forwarding from aggregation mode; confirm destination protocol and port; use reliable TCP where supported; verify filter logic and masking; authorize remote FAZ devices; check buffer headroom
selected.question_fingerprint: distinguish real-time forwarding from scheduled FAZ aggregation and determine why logs are delayed, filtered or held in buffer
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: source FAZ log stream -> forwarding profile/filter/mask -> TCP/UDP transport -> remote FAZ/syslog/CEF receiver

selected.lesson_subject: LACP trunk formation and member-selection behavior: aggregator mode, fallback and hash fields
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: config switch trunk -> LACP active/passive or static/fortinet-trunk mode -> aggregator selection by bandwidth/count -> per-flow port-selection criteria -> optional fallback-port and member withdrawal behavior
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: define trunk members and mode; negotiate LACP if active/passive; select eligible aggregator; hash source/destination MAC/IP to member; handle partner absence via fallback or member withdrawal policy
selected.failure_class: partner not negotiating; mismatched LACP mode/key; fallback hides peer misconfiguration; poor hash entropy causes uneven utilization; member withdrawal blocks traffic
selected.evidence_pattern: show switch trunk; LACP actor/partner state; per-member counters; port-selection criteria; link state and fallback member
selected.remediation_path: match LACP settings at both ends; verify actor/partner state; choose hash tuple that fits traffic diversity; configure fallback only for intentional non-LACP peer; validate min/max bundle and withdrawal behavior
selected.question_fingerprint: distinguish a formed LACP bundle from balanced traffic distribution and predict which flow tuple keeps traffic on one member
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: two peer switches -> LACP control exchange -> aggregator selection -> flow hash -> individual trunk member links

selected.lesson_subject: SSID VLAN pooling: AP-group assignment versus tunnel-mode client load balancing
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: SSID VAP VLAN pool -> optional AP-group-to-VLAN mapping or tunnel-mode client load balancer -> round-robin least-populated VLAN or hash selection -> generated SSID zone
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: define VLAN pool under VAP; create matching VLAN interfaces/networks/DHCP; choose wtp-group, round-robin or hash; AP association selects VLAN; client obtains address from selected VLAN
selected.failure_class: pool VLAN has no valid member; VLAN interface/DHCP missing; attempt to use load balancing in bridge mode; mistaken assumption hash and round-robin are equivalent
selected.evidence_pattern: show wireless-controller vap; SSID zone membership; client association VLAN; DHCP lease and VLAN interface counters
selected.remediation_path: verify every pool VLAN is valid and provisioned; use tunnel mode for load-balancing pools; distinguish AP-group mapping from client-count balancing; confirm DHCP and policy for each VLAN
selected.question_fingerprint: choose the right pool method for per-AP segmentation versus client load distribution and identify fallback to static VLAN
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: SSID VAP -> VLAN pool selector (AP group/round-robin/hash) -> SSID zone/VLAN interfaces -> DHCP scopes -> wireless clients

selected.lesson_subject: FortiNAC 9.4 User Organizational Unit LDAP mapping into User/Host Profiles and FSSO context
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: remote LDAP user object -> OU attribute mapping in FortiNAC User/Host Profile -> FSSO publication to FortiGate alongside FortiGate Device Tag and User Group
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: LDAP sync obtains user and OU membership; FortiNAC profile can match OU context; FSSO communicates user identity, group and device tag context to FortiGate for policy selection
selected.failure_class: OU not mapped or not synchronized; nested/renamed OU mismatch; FortiGate receives group/device tag but not expected OU context; policy assumes OU value is a network access policy field rather than FSSO identity metadata
selected.evidence_pattern: remote LDAP user record and OU; User/Host Profile mapping; FSSO connection/log; FortiGate FSSO user/group/device-tag view and matching firewall policy
selected.remediation_path: verify LDAP attribute and OU value are populated; map the correct OU field in User/Host Profile; verify FSSO publication and FortiGate receipt; align FortiGate identity-based policy with received context
selected.question_fingerprint: trace an OU-based identity classification from LDAP into FortiNAC and FSSO without confusing it with FortiNAC RADIUS VLAN policy matching
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: LDAP directory -> FortiNAC User/Host Profile OU mapping -> FSSO identity update -> FortiGate user/device-tag policy

selected.lesson_subject: IP phone voice VLAN provisioning: Local RADIUS attributes and MAC-notification-driven refresh
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: IP-phone host profile -> Network Access Policy -> Logical Network -> Local RADIUS attribute group (Tunnel-Medium-Type, Tunnel-Type, Tunnel-Private-Group-Id, Cisco-AVPair voice class) -> switch tagged voice VLAN
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: phone is profiled/registered; FortiNAC selects voice policy; RADIUS Access-Accept returns VLAN and voice attributes; switch places phone in voice VLAN; MAC notification traps can trigger revalidation on connect/disconnect
selected.failure_class: Local versus Proxy RADIUS mode confusion; missing policy; mismatched RADIUS shared secret; incorrect VLAN attribute group; noisy MAC notification traps
selected.evidence_pattern: RADIUS Access-Request/Accept attributes; switch port voice/data VLAN state; FortiNAC host profile/policy; MAC notification trap event timeline
selected.remediation_path: confirm Local RADIUS requirement; create profile/policy/logical network; use RFC VLAN attributes plus Cisco-AVPair; match shared secret; enable MAC traps only when real-time voice provisioning is required
selected.question_fingerprint: diagnose why an IP phone receives data VLAN but not voice VLAN by separating policy match, RADIUS attribute response and switch interpretation
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: IP phone -> access switch -> RADIUS Access-Request -> FortiNAC policy/attribute group -> Access-Accept -> tagged voice VLAN

selected.lesson_subject: Self-service password recovery with SMS or FortiToken verification and rate-limited portal workflow
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Authentication portal pre-login Password Reset option -> permitted verification methods -> per-user SMS/FortiToken recovery enrollment -> rate-limited recovery transaction -> LDAP/local password update
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: enable Password Reset and select verification methods in portal policy; configure user recovery options or LDAP sync rule; user requests reset; proves identity by SMS or FortiToken; reset operation updates account password
selected.failure_class: portal method disabled; user lacks recovery channel; SMS gateway or token delivery failure; LDAP permission/LDAPS constraint; rate limit reached
selected.evidence_pattern: portal pre-login configuration; user recovery options; SMS/token send and verification logs; LDAP bind/reset permissions; rate-limit response
selected.remediation_path: enable supported method in portal; provision user or remote LDAP sync recovery options; verify SMS delivery and FortiToken enrollment; confirm LDAPS/domain-join permissions; respect throttling before retry
selected.question_fingerprint: distinguish portal-wide verification methods from per-user recovery enrollment and identify why a user sees no SMS or token option
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: user portal reset request -> selected SMS/FortiToken factor -> recovery verification -> local/LDAP password update

selected.lesson_subject: Native RDP TCP forwarding mode: transport fallback and lost native RDP security controls
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: RDP Service secret -> TCP Forwarding option -> FortiPAM TCP tunnel consistent with Other clientType launcher instead of native RDP launcher integration
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: enable TCP forwarding for RDP secret; client establishes forwarded TCP path through FortiPAM; remote endpoint receives RDP stream; certificate revocation or legacy RDP protocol issue bypassed at the native launcher layer
selected.failure_class: native RDP launch fails certificate revocation check or protocol compatibility; operator enables TCP forwarding but assumes native RDP features still apply
selected.evidence_pattern: secret RDP Service configuration; launcher/client type; TCP forwarding session state; observed absence of RDP security level, Restricted Admin, Auto TOTP and clipboard block controls
selected.remediation_path: use TCP forwarding only for documented compatibility reasons; if native RDP controls are required, keep TCP forwarding disabled and fix certificate/protocol prerequisites; test with least privilege
selected.question_fingerprint: select TCP forwarding to bypass native-launch compatibility failure while recognizing which native RDP security features are no longer available
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiPAM RDP secret -> TCP forwarding tunnel -> target RDP service; native RDP feature-control branch omitted

selected.lesson_subject: FortiSIEM discovery orchestration: Range Scan, Smart Scan, cloud scans and Collector/Worker job placement
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: discovery entry type/range/root IP -> credential mapping -> Collector performs discovery when assigned; otherwise Supervisor discovers and distributes performance jobs to active Workers via weighted round robin
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: create discovery range and include/exclude criteria; map credentials by device type/domain; run or schedule scan; Collector/Supervisor discovers and returns CMDB objects; inspect results/errors/changes and assign ongoing monitoring jobs
selected.failure_class: wrong scan type/root IP; credential mapping absent or ambiguous; scan scope too broad; ping precheck suppresses non-ICMP hosts; Worker reassignment changes monitoring placement
selected.evidence_pattern: discovery Results/Errors/History/Changes; Collector assignment; CMDB host inventory; credential test; job distribution status
selected.remediation_path: select Range/Smart/L2/cloud scan appropriately; validate credentials and IP-to-credential mapping; use do-not-ping option where required; narrow include/exclude; schedule off-peak and inspect changes/errors
selected.question_fingerprint: distinguish Smart Scan topology traversal from Range Scan and diagnose why a Collector discovery result does not imply monitoring jobs are on the Supervisor
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: discovery definition -> Collector or Supervisor -> discovered devices/CMDB -> Worker performance-monitoring job assignment

selected.lesson_subject: FortiSASE external log forwarding: server access type, reliable TCP and TLS trust chain
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: Security PoP logs -> external server profile -> Public/Private reachability via internet or SPA FortiGate hub -> FAZ/syslog/CEF destination -> reliable TCP and optional TLS CA validation
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: enable external log forwarding; select server type and public/private access; define endpoint and port; choose forwarding frequency; for syslog enable reliable TCP and secure TLS; upload remote CA; verify Connecting to Connected
selected.failure_class: private server lacks SPA path; primary/secondary access-type constraint; TLS fails because remote CA missing; UDP/TCP reachability or cipher incompatibility
selected.evidence_pattern: FortiSASE connection status; selected access type; remote server listener; TLS certificate chain and CA; receiver log timestamps and per-log-type arrival
selected.remediation_path: match Public/Private to actual route; ensure SPA hub for private endpoint; import remote CA; use TCP for reliable delivery; validate server port/ciphers and allowed log types
selected.question_fingerprint: distinguish a network reachability failure from TLS trust failure and select the correct Public/Private server path
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiSASE Security PoP log sources -> forwarding profile -> public internet or SPA hub -> FAZ/syslog/CEF collector

selected.lesson_subject: Passive application-specific SLA measurement: per-service latency/jitter/loss from inspected live sessions
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: firewall policy passive-wan-health-measurement + application-control identification + passive/prefer-passive performance SLA + SD-WAN service passive-measurement per ISDB/application
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: enable passive measurements on policy and SD-WAN rule; classify traffic by ISDB/application signatures; collect live session metrics by application and member; compare SLA thresholds; steer subsequent flows based on per-application measured path quality
selected.failure_class: hardware offload left enabled; application classification missing; no live traffic for passive-only SLA; using active probe metrics as proxy for application performance
selected.evidence_pattern: diagnose sys link-monitor-passive admin list by-interface; per-rule SLA metrics; policy application-control profile; passive-measurement setting; interface session samples
selected.remediation_path: disable auto-asic-offload on participating policies; enable app-control classification; use passive or prefer-passive health check; generate representative app traffic; use active fallback where idle paths need measurement
selected.question_fingerprint: explain why a generic ping SLA is healthy while one application has poor latency and identify the policy/rule requirements for per-application passive measurement
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: application session -> firewall policy inspection -> passive metrics collector -> app-specific SLA per WAN member -> SD-WAN rule steering
